method: word-match over source reachable from the real entry points; a name shared with a method or local elsewhere reads as reached, so the orphan count is a lower bound

orphans.name: csrScale
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: graphLaplacian builds the normalized and random-walk forms directly from the adjacency rather than by scaling an existing CSR, so nothing in the sparse path needs a scaled copy; adding one would mean building a matrix to hand to a function that already computes what it needs.

orphans.name: structuredSurface
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Produces the exact form judge.ts's looksLikeStructuredTelemetry penalises: raw JSON carrying scce.surface.candidate.v1 reaching an answer is what that guard exists to catch. Artifacts are file-shaped (FileArtifact), so there is no structured-surface channel for it either. Wiring it would create surfaces the judge is built to downrank.

orphans.name: addMatrix
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Dense matrix arithmetic with no dense consumer left. The kernel's Laplacian path is sparse (graphLaplacian over CsrMatrix), and the heat/diffusion operators step vector-wise, so the natural-looking uses would materialise a dense matrix per step to replace an O(nnz) vector update.

orphans.name: scaleMatrix
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Same as addMatrix: the diffusion operators apply eta to the vector delta each step rather than scaling a matrix, and scaling one per step to match would allocate n^2 per iteration for no gain.

orphans.name: createAlignmentEngine
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: An IBM Model 1-style lexical aligner that trains from a parallel corpus of sentence pairs, and this system has no parallel corpus to train it on. The production translation lane is translationEngine.plan, which writes its own TranslationAlignmentRecords from each turn (putTranslationAlignment, production-turn-runtime) and reads them back as priorAlignments, so alignments accumulate from the system's own translations rather than from a bilingual corpus. Wiring this engine would add a second, competing alignment trainer fed by nothing.

orphans.name: clusterLanguageProfiles
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Merges MultilingualLanguageProfile records sharing a sourceClusterId. The production translation lane carries LanguageProfile from language memory, a different type built by a different path, so there is no set of these profiles anywhere in the runtime to cluster -- only translation.ts's own pairwise buildLanguageProfile calls, which produce exactly two and share no cluster.

orphans.name: createBulkIngestBatches
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Plans byte-range batches for a bulk-copy load path that does not exist: ingestion streams per file and writes per source version inside a transaction, so there is no caller to hand a batch plan to. Building that path is the ingest-throughput work (roughly 400-500 pages/hour today, ~6s per page in writes), a measured performance project rather than a wiring, and inventing a caller here would plan batches nothing executes.

orphans.name: createPredictionConstruct
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Requires a predictedSurface, and nothing in the runtime produces one. The turn computes forecast states and envelopes over the alpha trace, which are numeric, and turning a forecast into a stated surface needs the construction grammar that has never promoted from this corpus. The missing half is generation, not a call site.

orphans.name: predictionConstructNode
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Projects a PredictionConstruct into a construct graph node, so it cannot be reached before a prediction construct exists; see createPredictionConstruct.

orphans.name: createCanonicalJson
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: A factory returning { stringify: canonicalStringify } over a pure function every caller imports directly. There is no alternate canonical-JSON implementation to swap in and canonical form is a contract rather than a policy, so introducing an injection port to consume it would add indirection that enables nothing.

orphans.name: scoreRelationPotential
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Validates the model on every call, which is right for a single score and wrong for the only production use: scoreGraphEdgesWithRelationPotential freezes the model once and scores every edge against it. Routing that loop through here would re-validate per edge. Relation promotion, the other place a potential score would fit, decides by description length rather than by this model.

orphans.name: sparseDot
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: The only scorer over a SparseVector is the FTRL ranker, which already walks the entries to build the per-entry contribution breakdown its audit records, then sums that. Routing the sum through sparseDot would recompute every weight and throw the breakdown away, so the call site that looks right is strictly worse than what is there.

orphans.name: workingMemoryEntriesForTask
orphans.deliberatelyUnwired: Filters working memory by taskId, and the two id spaces do not meet. A turn writes entries under a turn-scoped id (task.turn.<episodeId>.candidate_selection) while the task resumption snapshot carries the program decomposition graph, whose node ids come from the program planner. Scoping the snapshot by that graph was tried and dropped every entry, emptying the summary; the caller already passes exactly the working memory it means to summarise.
